quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that you cannot see in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit starts right at the sign.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, you must slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply at an extreme angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead curves sharply (in this case, to the right). Slow down before reaching a sharp curve just like you would at an intersection turn.

questions.question: Driving at night requires increased caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Drivers cannot see as well at night. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever objects are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral quickly and press the brake firmly. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then turn when the path is clear.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous because it is harder to see, you may be blinded by headlights from other vehicles, and more drivers on the road may be tired or impaired.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are slippery or in poor condition to maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Warning of hazards ahead or nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning of hazards ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so they can see you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: You can ignore it in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black lettering.
A recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Speed signs on curves and turns show a recommended safe speed. You should never drive faster than this speed, especially in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller than cars and easier to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge their distance and speed. Always stay alert when near motorcycles.

questions.question: When can you NOT turn right on a solid red light?

options.text: When a pedestrian or vehicle is in the intersection.
When a walk signal is shown for a crossing.
When a sign says no right turn on red.

questions.explanation: You can turn right on red only if a sign does not prohibit it. You cannot turn right on red if a walk signal is displayed for the crossing, even if no pedestrians are there. You must also yield to any pedestrians or vehicles in the intersection before turning.

questions.question: What happens when a driver goes much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: They are a very safe driver.
They should not let cars behind them pass.
They may create a dangerous situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may create a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic flow is hazardous. On a two-lane road, if traffic backs up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles left toward the center. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: A solid edge line shows where the road ends. When this line angles toward the center of the road, it means the road narrows ahead.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign is always a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beam when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Speed up faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Speed up to match traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to traffic speed. Signal, look for an opening, and merge into traffic at the same speed as other vehicles.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn of railroad crossings. Yield to trains and never try to drive around the crossing gates.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:
questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to a blind person using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a red light is coming. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no gates or lights but with a crossbuck sign, you should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you see no train coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Wait for a flagger to signal you to proceed, if one is present.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, obey their instructions.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from:
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: If traffic signals are not working due to a power outage:

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the risk of a crash. If you drive faster than others, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, follow the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Parking is reserved for people with disabled permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown.
Lanes are reserved for buses and shared vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking is reserved for people with disabled permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disabled parking permits only.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle. You must show all three when stopped by police.
